# Agent Failure-Mode Taxonomy (gzkit)

> **Rule version:** `0.8.4` — the Reckless-action backstop names the rules that guard it (operator, 2026-11-08: *"fix what is stale"*); prior banners in [Rule Version History](../../docs/governance/rule-version-history.md#agent-failure-modesmd).

Patterns are maintained against the **current** frontier system cards — the registry-rotated set in `data/frontier_model_cards.json` (chore: `frontier-model-card-currency`), presently the Claude Fable 5.1 & Claude Mythos 5.1 System Card (§§ 2.3.3, 6.2.1, 6.4.2–6.4.5, 6.6.1), the Claude Opus 5.5 System Card (§§ 6.3.1, 6.4.1, 6.4.3–6.4.5, 6.5.1), and the GPT-6 Astra System Card (§§ 8.3.1, 8.6, 8.7, 8.8, 9.1–9.2) — and against repo-observed defects cited in the worked examples. Origin lineage lives in [Rule Version History](../../docs/governance/rule-version-history.md#agent-failure-modesmd), never in this rule. Cite by name when reviewing, filing defects, or extending the scorecard to route directly to the backstop. **Loading posture:** advisory vocabulary, not a mechanical gate — the defenses named in the Backstop column are the shared enforcement.

| Pattern | Definition | Backstop |
|---------|-----------|----------|
| **Safeguard circumvention** | Works around a guardrail instead of producing the evidence it asks for | Behavior Rules — the ledger-and-hooks rule; ARB receipts; § Gate Covenant (Gate 5 is universal) |
| **Reckless action** | Hard-to-reverse action without confirming authorization for this scope | Behavior Rules — the ask-when-unsure rule; the brief's Allowed Paths and DO IT RIGHT #11 (surgical changes): an action is denied unless the brief names it |
| **Fabrication** | Synthesized claim/receipt/attestation not observed from primary source | ARB receipt discipline; § Attestation (operator words verbatim, then evidence) |
| **Skipped cheap verification** | Pattern-matched incantation from training memory without running it | DO IT RIGHT 6g, #4; ARB receipt requirement |
| **Correction fails** | Correction received but not internalized or applied superficially | Behavior Rules — the `gz insights remember` rule; T1/T2/T3 invariants |
| **Dishonest when caught** | Post-hoc rationalization without quoting rule and conflicting directive verbatim | DO IT RIGHT 6h; verbatim-quoting requirement |
| **Hallucinated authorization** | Acts on a gate it *believes* was passed when no artifact records it — fabricates the precondition to itself, then proceeds sincerely | Gate 5 `--attestor` + non-empty `evidence.attestation_text`, ledger-written; cite the authorizing artifact, never recall it |
| **Security shortcut for expedience** | Trades a security or integrity property for convenience without surfacing the tradeoff | Behavior Rules — the commit-through-hooks rule (no `--no-verify`) and the push-back rule (cite the rule) |
| **Metagaming / gaming the gate** | Reasons about how the gate, validator, or grader will judge the work and shapes output to satisfy the check rather than the intent it proxies — user-facing summary omits what the reasoning admits | DO IT RIGHT #6 (tests assert semantics, not strings); Behavior Rules — the ledger-and-hooks rule (diagnose hook blocks, never work around); ARB receipts + Layer-2 ledger over agent narrative |

> See [`docs/governance/agent-contract-rationale.md` § Failure-mode worked examples](../../docs/governance/agent-contract-rationale.md#failure-mode-worked-examples) for worked examples, invocation patterns, the pattern-7 distinction from patterns 1/3, the pattern-7 provenance caveat, and promotion roadmap (GHIs #308–#312).

# Map-Not-Encyclopedia Doctrine (gzkit)

> **Rule version:** `0.14.0` — the rule also loads on the canon it governs (`.gzkit/corpus/**`, `.gzkit/rules/**`, `.gzkit/skills/**`), since the three generated surfaces are never edited by hand (RP-7 held ruling H13, operator, 2026-11-14: *"A: Keep, re-scope"*); version narrative in [Rule Version History](../../docs/governance/rule-version-history.md#agents-md-map-doctrinemd).

## Invariant

AGENTS.md MUST contain only (a) binding bullet rules (one bullet = one rule, ≤ 3 lines per bullet), (b) structured tables (Persona, Gate Covenant, OBPI kinds, canonical invocations, defect-fix routing thresholds), and (c) canonical-link references to deeper documentation at stable URLs under `docs/governance/`. AGENTS.md MUST NOT contain (i) multi-paragraph rationale prose (a paragraph over 5 lines without a binding-bullet anchor), (ii) worked examples or anti-pattern catalogs, (iii) "Why this is canon" / "Why X" coda blockquotes, (iv) narrative pedagogical sections, or (v) operative-claims expansions whose binding-bullet form already states the rule. CLAUDE.md inherits the same shape contract; `.claude/rules/*.md` inherit it with their per-file budget.

## Budget

The enforced budgets are the values in `data/instructions_files_budget.json`, read by `gz validate --instructions-files-budget`; this rule never restates them (a duplicated number drifts from what is enforced — the drift ADR-0.0.54 closeout corrected). The destination for AGENTS.md is the range in `docs/governance/agents-md-doctrine.md` § Budget targets, an ideal and a ceiling (operator rulings 2026-09-19); closing the distance lands under `ADR-0.35.0-canon-entry-corpus-landing` § Decision 3 (sections declare `corpus-owned` or `unowned`, the generator materializes owned sections, the unowned byte total is a decrease-only ratchet). Cite that ADR directly; its predecessors (`ADR-0.0.37`, GHI #533) are terminal.

Budgets are advisory until 1.0 (operator ruling 2026-08-17): every file is measured and each overrun reported with its distance and the `/gz-context-diet` pointer, but nothing blocks. The Codex delivery cap in `data/vendor-manifest.json` is a limit gzkit **sets** through the `.codex/config.toml` it generates, and any change to it is verified by observing what Codex actually delivered — `gz validate --instructions-files-budget` carries a codex-delivery witness for that (GHI #962). Raising the cap without re-observing delivery is the defect GHI #815 recorded.

## Shape enforcement

`gz validate --agents-md-map-conformance` asserts, fail-closed: no paragraph in AGENTS.md over 5 lines without a binding-bullet anchor; no subsection title in the prohibited set; every `See [text](path)` link resolves. File size is reported against the budget file, advisory only. Violations emit a `RemediationPayload` with `recovery: /gz-context-diet`.

Bringing an over-budget surface back into trim is the `instructions-files-diet` chore's job, on a cadence or on demand; ordinary sessions add to sources (`gz content remember`) and never resize a render surface.

## Attestation granularity

Operator ruling 2026-08-17: **the discriminator is whether CANON changed — never whether a file was written.** A rendition is a Layer-3 derived view; the corpus is Layer-1. Attestation attaches to the canon change and to completed OBPI/ADR work, never to the projection.

| Act | Disposition |
|---|---|
| Re-render of **unchanged** canon | No attestation; the corpus fingerprint is unmoved and `--rendition-floor-coherence` proves the invariant floor survived. The chore completes it. |
| Adding a corpus entry (`gz content remember`) | Attested — recorded provenance |
| Removing an entry (`gz content retire`) | Attested — recorded provenance |
| Trim / compression to fit a delivery cap | Invites operator review: it changes what canon looks like, not what canon is |

- A GHI needs no attestation (operator verbatim: *"I only attest to completed obpi/adr work"*); the GHI is the work order and the receipt.
- Do not call a build step "Gate 5." The content surface's attestation is named CORPUS ATTESTATION. Gate 5 is OBPI/ADR completion attestation (ADR-0.0.36) and nothing else; the noun is `corpus`, not `rendition`, because the attestable subject is the corpus (GHI #822).
- Attestation on add/remove is recorded provenance, never a blocking gate: *"Capture must never be blocked: losing the operator's words is strictly worse than a red tree"* (`ADR-0.35.0` § Decision 7).
- The transport never gates the attestation: a ruling relayed verbatim via `--attestation-text` IS the attestation; "the operator is not at a terminal" never stops a chore.

(Advisory — no witness holds it, and the verbs carry the granularity only in part: `gz content remember` takes no `--attestor`, only a `--witness` recorded as provenance; `gz content retire` requires `--attestor` only when the retirement moves invariant-tier liveness; `gz content commit` requires `--attestor` and `--attestation-text` only when the corpus moved since that consumer's last committed rendition (GHI #821). Reclassify when the verbs carry the granularity.)

## Writing levers

Apply these when writing or trimming an `AGENTS.md` corpus entry, `CLAUDE.md`, a rule or a skill description. (Advisory — whether a sentence steers is settled by running the surface, not by reading it.)

- **Two loads.** Always-loaded text costs context on every turn; material behind a pointer costs the operator the memory that it exists. Spend context on what every task needs.
- **Branch test.** Inline what every task needs; put what only some tasks reach behind a pointer (a path-scoped rule, a skill, a doc). A rule that must steer every turn stays inline in full.
- **Pointer wording.** A pointer says what the material is and when to reach it. When a needed target is being missed, sharpen the pointer before inlining the material.
- **Positive target.** State the behavior wanted; keep a prohibition only as a hard guardrail with no positive phrasing, paired with the target.
- **No-op hunt.** A sentence the model already obeys by default pays load to say nothing; delete it. The default is model-relative, so a disagreement is settled by a run.
- **Single source, and the environment counts.** One home per meaning. Restating what a config file, `--help` or the directory layout already says is a cache that goes stale; keep the convention, the reason, the gotcha.
- **Co-location.** A concept's rule, its caveats and its witness sit under one heading.
- **Leading words.** Reuse gzkit's established terms (witness, canon, derived view, coupled surface, direct fix) as tokens; do not re-explain them.
- **A skill description is a pointer that never unloads.** A skill the agent need not reach on its own is user-invoked (`disable-model-invocation: true`) and costs no context.

## Related

- `docs/governance/agents-md-doctrine.md` — canonical expansion; `docs/governance/agent-contract-rationale.md` — lift target
- `.gzkit/skills/gz-context-diet/SKILL.md` — the operator-facing procedure; `data/instructions_files_budget.json` — the enforced values
- `ADR-0.0.54-agents-md-map-not-encyclopedia-doctrine` — parent ADR

# Mode Contract (gzkit)

> **Rule version:** `0.1.2` — the fail-safe default restored after the 0.1.1 compression (operator review, 2026-10-28); advisory until RO-13 lands its witness.

Every new control, module, skill, rule or surface carries the two-way mode contract from its first commit: operator, 2026-10-26, *"an overarching design requirement permanently and always with everything we build"*. A design without it is incomplete. Retrofitting what exists is RO-13's program.

## What a new control declares

1. **Its behavior** at the operational condition, the **hangar** level and the **drydock** level: on, advisory or off. The condition is on only when the marker is present, parses, is bound to an open `mx_session_opened` and is not exiting. Anything else is the operational condition.
2. **Its MEL entry:** level per standby level, (M) bypass procedure, (O) limitation, placard, restore condition and deadline (at the latest the exit re-run), self-test interval, accepted state.
3. **Its built-in self-test:** suitable when its latest result passed within the declared interval, otherwise inoperative under its (O) limitation.

`GATE5_INVARIANTS` is never listed. The level is applied at the place of call, never by the declaration. Until RO-13 builds the declaration shapes (decorator, Markdown MEL block, `gzkit.mx.alarms` arguments), state the contract in the design artifact's § Mode Contract.

**Advisory: no mechanical witness yet.** RO-13's shrink-only baseline of controls with no MEL entry, closed at zero, is the planned witness. Record: `docs/rnd/contractor-kit.md` § *the mode contract is a permanent design requirement for everything gzkit builds*.

# Skill & Surface Sync (gzkit)

> **Rule version:** `0.14.1` — § Surface layout describes the drift report sync actually gives, and the classifier gives `project_local` to skills as well as chores (operator, 2026-11-08: *"fix what is stale"*); prior narrative in [Rule Version History](../../docs/governance/rule-version-history.md#skill-surface-syncmd).

## Non-negotiable rules

1. **Edit `.gzkit/` first.** `.gzkit/skills/` and `.gzkit/rules/` are canonical; every other copy is generated.
2. **Bump the version on every edit.** Do not edit a skill without bumping its `skill-version` frontmatter, nor a rule without its body-level marker; do not skip sync because two files look the same (it also updates manifests and registrations). Skills: `metadata.skill-version`, a quoted `X.Y.Z` string nested under `metadata:` (a top-level `skill-version:` is invisible to `skills_audit.py`; presence is enforced, `SKA-METADATA-SKILL-VERSION-MISSING`). Rules: the body-level `<!-- rule-version: X.Y.Z -->` comment right after the frontmatter plus the visible `> **Rule version:** \`X.Y.Z\`` block quote with a one-sentence rationale; `RuleFrontmatter` is `extra="forbid"` and rejects `skill-version:` on a rule. Minor for a governance or procedure change, patch for wording or tooling.
3. **Run sync after every edit.** `uv run gz agent sync control-surfaces` writes the wheel copy at `src/gzkit/<surface>/` and every enabled vendor's mirror in one invocation.
4. **Never edit vendor mirrors directly.** Read the roster from `.gzkit.json` § `vendors`, never from a list here — a transcribed roster went stale when Copilot was dropped (GHI #921).
5. **Never edit `src/gzkit/<surface>/` directly.** `src/gzkit/{skills,rules,personas,templates}/` are derived; only `sync_pkg_surfaces` writes them.
6. **`skill-version` bumps require `last_reviewed` bumps in the same edit (skills only).** Set `last_reviewed:` to today's date whenever `skill-version` moves — the 90-day staleness audit (`DEFAULT_MAX_REVIEW_AGE_DAYS`, `src/gzkit/skills_audit.py`) reads it, and a version bump without it silently disarms that signal. Rules carry no `last_reviewed:`.

## Surface layout

| Canonical (edit here) | Pkg copy (generated) | Vendor mirrors (generated) | Version marker |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.gzkit/skills/` | `src/gzkit/skills/` | `<surface_root>/skills/` per enabled vendor | `metadata.skill-version` |
| `.gzkit/rules/` | `src/gzkit/rules/` | `<surface_root>/rules/` or the vendor's `instruction_format` path | `<!-- rule-version -->` + block quote |
| `.gzkit/personas/` | `src/gzkit/personas/` | `<surface_root>/personas/` | none |
| `.gzkit/templates/` | `src/gzkit/templates/` | none (scaffold-time only) | none |
| `.gzkit/chores/<slug>/` | `src/gzkit/chores/<slug>/` (canonical class only) | none | none |

Sync compares no versions: it rewrites every mirror from canon, so a hand edit to a mirror is lost at the next sync. The drift report is `gz validate --surfaces`: *"Generated surface is out of sync with canonical state. Run `uv run gz agent sync control-surfaces` to repair."* (`validate_pkg/sync_parity.py`). Before running that sync, carry any mirror edit worth keeping into `.gzkit/` and bump its version; flag one whose origin is unclear for human review. Full resolution design: [Skill-Surface-Sync Rationale](../../docs/governance/skill-surface-sync-rationale.md).

## Bootstrap semantics (`gz init`)

After `gz init`, the adopter's `.gzkit/<surface>/` is the canonical source and rule 1 binds from then on; the wheel's package surface is the one-time bootstrap source. Repair-mode `gz init` is idempotent (`skip_existing=True`); `--force` wipes and re-copies. Retired-slug filtering, scaffolding order and the `gz init --update` roadmap: [Rationale § Bootstrap semantics](../../docs/governance/skill-surface-sync-rationale.md#bootstrap-semantics-gz-init).

## Retirement policy (delete-on-retire, binding)

A superseded or consolidated skill's directory is deleted from every surface root — `.gzkit/skills/`, `src/gzkit/skills/`, each enabled vendor's `<surface_root>/skills/` — in the same commit or OBPI that introduces its successor. No `lifecycle_state: retired` stub survives. Rationale (GHI #464): [Rationale § Retirement policy](../../docs/governance/skill-surface-sync-rationale.md#retirement-policy-delete-on-retire).

A retired rule leaves the same way. Its doctrine moves first, to a named home: a skill that runs when the rule binds, a doc under `docs/governance/`, an `AGENTS.md` entry, or the failure message of the witness that enforces it. Retiring never deletes doctrine. In the commit that retires the rule:

- delete `.gzkit/rules/<name>.md`, then sync, which removes the vendor mirrors. Sync never removes the package copy, so delete `src/gzkit/rules/<name>.md` by hand. That is the one exception to rule 5, and it lasts until GHI #1316 lands;
- remove its entry from `data/distribution_baseline_manifest.json` and its row from the Coverage Ledger of `docs/governance/advisory-rules-audit.md`, and re-point or retire the scorecard rows that cite it;
- re-point every test, validator message, doc link and `.gzkit/chores/registry.json` target that names the rule's path.

A test behind an attested REQ that reads the rule is repaired at the surface (`AGENTS.md` § OBPI Acceptance Protocol, attested REQ whose subject a later ruling retired); one whose REQ asserts the file exists goes to the operator first. **Advisory in part:** `gz validate --distribution` refuses a baseline entry left behind, but sync never removes the package copy (GHI #1316) or an adopter's copy, and no witness flags an orphaned ledger row (GHI #1317).

## Canonical surface class-classifier

Every file under a canonical surface (`src/gzkit/{chores,rules,skills,personas,templates}/`) is exactly one class (OBPI-0.0.32-13/-15):

| Class | Definition | Byte-parity | Sync |
|---|---|---|---|
| **canonical** | operator-authored content present at `.gzkit/<surface>/` | required | `.gzkit/ → src/gzkit/`; in the wheel and the baseline manifest |
| **package_only** | Python modules and support files with no `.gzkit/` counterpart (`__init__.py`, `_scaffolder.py`), and a retired skill the wheel still carries | exempt | never propagated to `.gzkit/` |
| **runtime_state** | per-run logs, receipts, proofs | exempt | never synced either way |
| **project_local** *(chores and skills)* | a chore whose `registry.json` entry declares `"projectLocal": true`, or a skill whose `SKILL.md` frontmatter declares `project_local: true` (GHI #915) | exempt | never shipped in the wheel or scaffolded by `gz init` |

Declare a project-local chore with `"projectLocal": true` in `.gzkit/chores/registry.json`, and a project-local skill with `project_local: true` in its `SKILL.md` frontmatter — the property is declared, never inferred, and the shipped `registry.json` is filtered so the wheel never advertises a chore it does not carry (GHI #728). `gz validate --distribution` and `sync_pkg_surfaces` both read the per-surface `_classify_<surface>_file` helpers. Per-surface default classes and the classifier matrix: [Rationale § Class-classifier reference](../../docs/governance/skill-surface-sync-rationale.md#class-classifier-reference).
